wu: Warm-up: Recycle Relay! Teams race to sort picture cards into bins labeled 'Paper', 'Plastic', 'Glass'. Students shout 'This is paper!' or 'This is plastic!' as they sort.
wuAlt: Alternative warm-up 1: Earth Day Pictionary—draw a recycling symbol, a tree, or a litter bin for teammates to guess in English.
Alternative warm-up 2: 'I Spy with my little eye something you can recycle'—students guess objects in the classroom.
pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of recyclable items (bottle, can, newspaper) and trash (banana peel, plastic bag). Model 'What is it? It is a bottle.' and 'Can you recycle it? Yes, I can.' Check understanding with thumbs up/down.
presAlt: Alternative presentation 1: Use a story about a child cleaning up a park—point to items and ask 'Recycle or trash?'
Alternative presentation 2: Demonstrate with realia—hold up a bottle and ask 'Can you recycle this?' students answer.
prac: Guided practice: Pair work—students take turns asking 'What is it?' and 'Can you recycle it?' using flashcards. Monitor and correct pronunciation, especially 'can' and 'recycle'.
pracAlt: Alternative practice 1: 'Recycle Sort' game—teams race to sort word cards into correct bins, shouting the category.
Alternative practice 2: 'First, then...' drill—'First, I find a bottle. Then, I put it in the bin.'
ls: Listening slot: Play a recording of a teacher saying 'I can recycle a can. I cannot recycle a banana peel.' Students hold up the correct picture card. Checks if they distinguish recyclable from non-recyclable.
re: Reactivation game: 'Litter Tag'—one student is 'litter' (holds a trash card), others chase them to tag and say 'Put it in the bin!' to make them 'recycle'.
prod: Production task: Plant-a-seed craft—students follow 'First, put soil in the pot. Then, put a seed in.' in pairs. They take turns giving instructions, using target language.
rw: Reading and writing slot: Trace and copy sentences like 'I can recycle a bottle.' and 'This is paper.' Then complete sentence starters like 'I can recycle ____.' with words from a word bank.
st: Story/Song + goodbye: Read 'The Earth Day Helpers' story with repetitive phrases. End with 'Goodbye Song' (tune of 'Twinkle Twinkle')—'Goodbye friends, goodbye friends, see you next time, goodbye!' followed by sticker chart and high-five line.
g: Teams race to sort picture cards into bins labeled 'Paper', 'Plastic', 'Glass'.
Draw a recycling symbol, tree, or litter bin for teammates to guess in English.
Students take turns giving instructions like 'First, find a bottle. Then, recycle it.'
One student is 'litter', others tag them and say 'Put it in the bin!'
Follow 'First, put soil in the pot. Then, put a seed in.' in pairs.
diff: Fast finishers: Draw 3 more things to recycle and write sentences.
Support: Trace the sentences with dotted lines and match to pictures.
hw: Homework 1: Find 3 things at home to recycle and name them in English.
Homework 2: Draw a picture of you recycling and write one sentence about it.
Homework 3: Teach a family member how to sort recycling in English.
tip: Use Moroccan context—relate recycling to local cleanliness drives or the Green March spirit of community action. Celebrate with stickers for effort, not just accuracy.
